summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, ICD placement, diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for acute on chronic shortness of breath and orthopnea. The symptoms were attributed to an exacerbation of congestive heart failure, supported by elevated BNP, bibasilar crackles, and radiographic evidence of mild pulmonary edema. He was treated with intravenous furosemide and supplemental oxygen, with improvement in symptoms and a reduction in weight to his dry weight of 176 pounds. His renal function, initially impaired with a creatinine of 1.6, improved to 1.4 by discharge. Lisinopril was not restarted due to residual orthostatic hypotension and elevated creatinine. His diabetes was managed with insulin during admission, and Januvia was resumed at discharge. He experienced non-sustained ventricular tachycardia on telemetry but remained stable. He was discharged home with instructions on weight monitoring, fluid and sodium restriction, and follow-up with cardiology and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
